question.worked_solution:
We use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{7}\frac{1}{4\sqrt{2{sin}^{2}⁡x+x+2{cos}^{2}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{2}^{7}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+2({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{2}^{7}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+2\cdot 1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{2}^{7}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x+2}\,{|}_{2}^{7} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{7+2}-\sqrt{2+2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{9}-\sqrt{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3-2) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
